land.text: Zhetysu (Jetisu), the basin of the Seven Rivers with Suyab

predecessors.note: Taken in 766, not at the 742 birth: 'In 766, after they overran the Türgesh in Jetisu, the Karluk tribes formed a Khanate under the rule of a Yabghu' (Karluks page). The 742 core was the Karluk tribal country, nobody's land.

land.text: the whole Qarlugs shape of 840 (Zhetysu): 'When the Yenisei Kyrgyz destroyed the Uyghur Khaganate in 840 the Karluk yabghu declared himself khagan as Bilge Kul Qadir Khan'

successors.note: The Karluk Yabghu page describes this act as forming the Kara-Khanid Khanate; the Kara-Khanid page gives 'Established: 840'. Cliopatria keeps a Qarlugs row to 849 and starts its Kara-Khanids row in 850 on a shape that contains all 1,348 Qarlugs cells.

capitals.name: Suyab (Ak-Beshim)
capitals.note: The Karluks 'occupied Suyab and transferred their capital there' in 766; the Karluks page later names Balasagun as the Karluk capital without a date (the Kara-Khanid page: Balasagun 942-1130). Coordinates from the gazetteer. The seat before 766 is not on the page.

correction.text: the Karluk country 'between the Altai and the eastern shore of Lake Balkhash', the Black Irtysh and the Tarbagatai Mountains

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 742-765: Cliopatria's first Qarlugs shape begins in 793. The Karluk Yabghu page (infobox '742-840') has Karluk tribes first named 'in the area between the Altai and the eastern shore of Lake Balkhash'; the Karluks page puts them at 'the regions of Kara-Irtysh (Black Irtysh) and the Tarbagatai Mountains west of the Altay Mountains'. They are Uyghur vassals from 746.

keyframe_review.note: 793-839, 407,815 km2 (1,348 cells): Zhetysu (1,112 of the 1,435 cells of the gazetteer's Semirechye), Kyrgyzstan's Chu and Talas side (321 of 660 cells) and the Kazakh foothills; no infobox area on the Karluk Yabghu or Karluks page, so no comparison. The homeland of the Irtysh and Tarbagatai is not in the shape; the Karluks page says they 'spread from the valley of the river Kerlyk along the Irtysh River' (undated), so it is added.

correction.text: years only: from 840 this land is the Kara-Khanid Khanate (kara-khanids), the same Karluk polity under the title khagan

keyframe_review.note: 840-849: the state ends in 840 on the Karluk Yabghu page (infobox '742-840'; the yabghu declares himself khagan as Bilge Kul Qadir Khan and forms the Kara-Khanid Khanate; Kara-Khanid page 'Established: 840', Bilge Kul Qadir Khan (840-893)). The 840 shape is the Kara-Khanids' first shape (their 850 shape contains all 1,348 cells).

region.text: the Karluk country 'between the Altai and the eastern shore of Lake Balkhash', the Black Irtysh and the Tarbagatai Mountains

ledger.note: 742: the Karluk yabghu appears in the Altai-Balkhash country. 'Saɣ Yabghu: named in 742 by Basmyl Khagan Ashina Shi', later defeated by a Karluk-Uyghur coalition; infobox '742-840'. The page describes the tribes' area and does not date a founding; 742 is the infobox year.

region.text: Zhetysu (Jetisu), the basin of the Seven Rivers with Suyab

ledger.note: 766: the Karluks take Zhetysu. 'In 766, after they overran the Türgesh in Jetisu, the Karluk tribes formed a Khanate under the rule of a Yabghu' and 'occupied Suyab and transferred their capital there'; Kara-Khanid page: 'By 766, the Karluks had forced the submission of the Turgesh'.
766: the Karluks move their capital to Suyab, the Türgesh city on the Chu.

region.text: Futu Valley (Fu-tu valley), location not given on the page

ledger.note: 789: the Karluks annex the Futu Valley. 'The Karluks took this opportunity to encroach on Uyghur territory and annexed Futu Valley' (when Külüg succeeded). No location on the page; the placeholder is in Dzungaria where the Karluks page puts them (Tarbagatai). The Karluks then fought beside Tibet at Beiting in 791 and were beaten.

840: the Karluk yabghu becomes khagan. 'When the Yenisei Kyrgyz destroyed the Uyghur Khaganate in 840' the yabghu declared himself khagan as Bilge Kul Qadir Khan, forming the Kara-Khanid Khanate; the Karluks page: 'Karluk independence ended around 840', 'abandoning the old title Yabghu, to take on the new title of Khagan'.

wars.name: Uyghur-Karluk revolt against the Second Turkic Khaganate
wars.outcome: The Karluks revolted with the Uyghurs and Basmyls in 742; after the Basmyls took Ötüken in 744 a Uyghur-Karluk alliance defeated them; the Karluks then submitted to the Uyghurs (746).
wars.note: Karluks page: 'in about 745, and established a new tribal confederation with the Uygur and Basmyl tribes'.

wars.name: Karluk conquest of the Türgesh in Zhetysu

zones.text: Zhetysu (Jetisu), the basin of the Seven Rivers with Suyab

wars.outcome: The Karluks migrated west into Zhetysu (from 744) and in 766 overran the Türgesh, took Suyab and formed a Yabghu khanate.
wars.note: The Uyghur page: 'Hostilities between the Uyghurs and Karluks then forced the Karluks to migrate west into Zhetysu' (744). The start year is a placeholder: no page dates the fighting.

wars.name: Uyghur-Tibetan wars over the Tarim and Dzungaria
wars.outcome: The Karluks annexed the Futu Valley (789), fought with Tibet and lost to the Uyghurs at Beiting (791); the Uyghurs then took Gaochang (792).
wars.note: The Karluks' share of the war is two sentences on the Uyghur page; the Tibetan Empire page does not mention them in these years.

certainty.note: A tribal khanate of the steppe and the Chu-Ili valleys; no page gives a frontier.

notes:
Pages opened for this state: Karluks, Karluk Yabghu (the first URL tried, Karluk_Yabghu_State, returned 404; Karluk_Yabgu_State loaded and is titled 'Karluk Yabghu'), plus the Uyghur Khaganate and Kara-Khanid Khanate pages opened for the neighbours (4 pages; budget 1-2 for 2 shapes, exceeded by the two neighbour pages).
Cliopatria's wikipedia title for this row, 'Mongol invasion of Central Asia', is wrong for the state; the state article is Karluk Yabghu (infobox 742-840). Wikidata Q2330335 is Cliopatria's and was not checked.
One polity or two: the Karluk Yabghu page says the yabghu's 840 title change 'formed the Kara-Khanid Khanate', and the Kara-Khanid page begins in 840; Cliopatria has two rows (Qarlugs 793-849, Kara-Khanids 850-1045 with an 850 shape that contains all 1,348 Qarlugs cells). The brief keeps them as separate dossiers; I split them at 840 (the Cliopatria Qarlugs 840-849 shape is marked wrong here and added to kara-khanids as a new keyframe). If the colour agent treats them as one family, they should share it (successors claiming continuity share the family); a merge is for the reviewer.
Vassal years: the Karluks were Uyghur vassals from 746 (Karluk Yabghu page: 'submitted to the Uyghurs in 746'); that relation is carried as vassal_start/vassal_end events in the uyghur-khaganate ledger (counterpart qarlugs), not here. Karluks and Uyghurs: the Karluks page says the Karluks were 'forcibly incorporated into the Toquz Oghuz tribal confederation' and 'independence ended around 840'; the Karluk Yabghu page has the yabghu declare himself khagan in 840. The pages do not agree on when the Uyghur overlordship ended; 766 is a bridging judgement (confidence 1).
Cliopatria's Qarlugs shape starts in 793 and the Uyghur row holds Zhetysu until 792; the Uyghur dossier here removes Zhetysu from the Uyghur shape and carries it as a Türgesh vassal tint to 765.
The Futu valley (789) has no location on the page. Missing: the Karluks' Fergana lands (Karluks page: 'The Arabs dislodged the Karluks from Fergana', no year) are not drawn.
